title: SimpleRobot Programming Manual
subtitle: Blocks and Simple Robot Script — concepts, instruction reference, functions and error codes

figures.caption: One program, two views: the app edits it, the controller stores, checks and runs it.
Blocks and text are two views of the same stored program. Switching views never loses a field or a step id.
Program kinds: a main program calls routines and starts background programs.
Where a variable lives: the global store is shared by every running program; a program's variables (and its routines' parameters) belong to its run.

Coordinate frames. Left (top view): the world frame and a local frame (Fixture1) offset and turned 15°; a point taught in the local frame moves with it. Right (side view): the tool frame puts the TCP at the gripper tip.
How a move target is built: the base target, then offset, then override, all in the active (or step) local frame; the tool offset applies in the tool frame at the end.
A grid addresses cells by [row, col] or by index (row-major: index = row × columns + col). A stack addresses slots base + index × offset.
Move Linear keeps the tool on a straight line; Move Joint moves every joint proportionally, so the tool follows a curve — usually faster in open space.
A move ramps up at accel, cruises at speed, and ramps down at decel. A short move never reaches full speed (dashed). Program speeds are scaled by the speed override × Set Speed Factor.
Without blending the robot stops exactly on each point. With a blend radius it rounds the corner inside the radius and never stops.
Move Arc follows the circle through the start, the via point and the end. It is cut into chords within tolerance= of the true arc and run as one continuous path.
Jump (side view): lift straight up to zStart, traverse to above the target at zEnd, lower onto the target. z= sets both heights; the heights are absolute Z values.
A move with a stop condition: the condition is checked every tick. stop ends the move where it is; record lets it finish and stores the pose where the condition first held.
Set Output with pulse=250ms. blocking=on holds the program until the output has flipped back; without it the next step starts at once and the flip-back happens in the background.
Wait until <condition>, timeout=5s. If the input comes on in time the program continues; otherwise timedOut= is set to 1 and onTimeout decides: continue (default) or fail with waitTimeout.
if / elif / else: conditions are tested top to bottom; the first that holds runs its branch, then execution continues after end.
switch evaluates its value once and runs the first case with an equal value (no fall-through), else default.
The three loop forms. break leaves the loop at once; continue skips to the next pass.

try retry=2: a catchable failure abandons the body and runs it again until the retries are used up; then the catch steps run with the message and code. Fatal errors and codes not in only=(…) go outward.
A catchable error travels outward from the failing step — through loops, branches and called routines — to the nearest Try that catches its code. With none, the program ends with Error.
Calling a routine: in / inout arguments are evaluated in the caller, then copied into the parameters; when the routine ends (or returns), out / inout parameters are copied back.
Program states. Stop, a Pause Program step, a breakpoint or step mode all pause the run (Stopped) with its place kept; Continue resumes, Step runs one step and pauses again.
A background program runs beside the main program. It shares global variables and IO, skips motion, tool and homing steps, and can be stopped or waited for.
RunVision frame=: positions in pixels (origin top-left, y down), normalized 0–1, or robot millimetres on the camera's calibration plane.
A plugin is a separate process the controller starts. It connects back over a local WebSocket and contributes steps, expression functions and live properties.

The Blocks editor on a phone.
The Move Linear step editor: target, then optional speed, offsets, blending and a stop condition.
The Prompt step editor: message, title, buttons and the result variable.
